value.evidence: Draft A frames the post as a report about someone else's dated experiment ('I came across a 2025 Reddit post'), creating distance from the actual problem and weakening community engagement. It asks a generic comparative question without grounding it in the poster's own constraints or motivation. Draft B directly owns the hardware setup and motivation ('I'm exploring inference options'), explicitly acknowledges the inconclusive prior data (F4), names specific quantization methods the poster is actually considering (F6), and transparently flags missing information (ROCm/driver versions, detailed setups) that would help respondents give targeted advice. Draft B preserves all key facts (F1–F4, F6) while A only uses F1–F2. Draft B's framing—'since available reports lack info'—demonstrates credibility by acknowledging limitations rather than presenting archived observations as timeless facts. Both avoid forbidden claims, but B's specificity about quantization methods, multi-GPU utilization, and configuration details gives the community concrete angles to respond to, whereas A's 'hints at notable speed differences' is vague and doesn't invite actionable contribution.
